messages:
maria: FYI: seeing p99 tail spikes on text-gen around 18:00 PST, some requests hit ~2.2s. SLO is 1.5s so this is causing a few errors to flip to degradation.
raj: I profiled a few of the traces — looks like kernel selection churn + a KV-prefix eviction when batch depth grows beyond 7. KV eviction pushes fallback to the slower kernel path.
tyler: can you paste the flamegraph id?
raj: flame://2026-03-16/kv-evict-18h-01 (attached in thread). Peak shows memcopy + kernel-recompile windows. Also saw microbatch depth jump to 12 during spikes.
eva: is this the same regression we saw last month or a new pattern?
raj: different. Last month was a quantization kernel regression. This time it's workload-driven: a noisy cohort of long-concat prompts causing microbatches to accumulate and trigger aggressive prefix eviction.
maria: thinking immediate mitigation options: 1) reduce max microbatch depth on hot shards 2) enforce max_tokens cap per request 3) change eviction policy to LRU-age biased (keep KV for recent prefixes) 4) probabilistic tail-shedding for queued microbatches.
tyler: +1 to a short-term cap. Lowering max_tokens from 1024 -> 512 on the public route would blunt the long concat cases without touching models.
eva: what about kernel routing heuristics? if we detect long prefix lengths, route to a kernel optimized for long-seq (avoid recompile). But need careful perf testing.
raj: here's a minimal runtime config I sketched to try in canary (shard-local config):
```json
{
  "batching": {
    "max_microbatch_depth": 6,
    "max_inflight_per_shard": 8,
    "microbatch_timeout_ms": 80
  },
  "kv_cache": {
    "eviction_policy": "age_lru",
    "reserve_windows": 4
  },
  "tail_protections": {
    "probabilistic_shed": true,
    "shed_threshold_ms": 1100
  },
  "request_caps": {
    "max_tokens_per_request": 512,
    "truncate_mode": "suffix_truncate"
  }
}
```
maria: That looks reasonable. How do we measure tradeoffs? Need p95/p99 delta vs throughput. Target: p99 < 1.5s, p95 no more than +10% latency, throughput drop < 7%.
tyler: I'll run a synthetic sweep: baseline QPS 600, vary max_microbatch_depth [4,6,8] and cap [256,512,1024]. Collect p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. Command I'll use: `./tools/loadtest --route public-gen --qps 600 --duration 5m --profile flame.svg`
raj: Also enable short-term profiling on the canary: `./profiling/collect --target shard-3 --duration 60s --labels kv,compile`
eva: We should also add a fast fallback policy: if kernel recompile time > 200ms for 3 consecutive microbatches, fall back to stable-kernel (even if slightly slower per-token) to avoid compounding latency.
maria: agree. Ops runbook: 1) deploy config to 10% traffic canary at 09:00 UTC 2) monitor p95/p99 + kernel-recompile rate + kv-eviction events 3) if p99 < 1.5s and throughput drop < 7% after 10m, increase to 50% 4) rollback on any error spike or throughput drop > 10%.
sre-bot: Canary started: config-id c-20260316-001 on route public-gen (10% traffic).
tyler: initial canary numbers after 5m: p50 unchanged, p95 +6%, p99 fell from 2.2s -> 1.4s, tokens/sec -5%. Looks promising.
raj: profiling from canary shows KV evictions down ~70%, and kernel-recompile events fell to near-zero. Good sign.
eva: any negative side-effects? truncated responses?
tyler: we did see ~0.6% of responses reach the max_tokens cap and get truncated; qualitatively checks show most were noisy concatenations. We can add a user-facing warning for the rare truncation and an endpoint param to opt-out.
maria: action items: raj implement age_lru on staging and add the kernel-fallback heuristic, tyler run the full sweep and roll canary to 50% if stable, eva craft messaging about opt-out param and support note, I'll schedule a follow-up retro tomorrow.
raj: I'll open a short PR with the config and the fallback patch, tag for quick review.
type: thumbs: Maria: :thumbsup:
maria: thanks team. If we still see residual tail at 50% we'll experiment with probabilistic shedding thresholds and microbatch_timeout tuning.
